clue.text: Frequently lacking strength both home and away, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak tells us the phrase built from the clue is said aloud and heard as another phrase

parts.words: lacking strength both home and away
parts.note: lacking strength is weak; home is in and away is out, so the phrase is weak in, weak out

explanation.surface: A football team that is feeble in every match, whether playing at home or on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' marks the sound-alike: WEAK IN WEAK OUT, said aloud, sounds like the phrase meaning regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something happening every week without a break, hence frequently or habitually.

clue.text: With renewed energy and determination, you'll get thinner

indicators.note: renewed suggests the letters of the word With are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
spirit is courage or determination

explanation.surface: Advice that zeal and resolve will help you slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renewed' rearranges WITH to WHIT, then E is added. 'thinner' looks like slimmer but is the noun: a solvent for paint.
explanation.definitionFit: This solvent is the standard liquid used to thin oil paint and clean brushes.

clue.text: Animal, terribly lean, finally died

indicators.note: terribly signals that the word lean is to be mangled into another order
finally picks out the closing letter of the word died

explanation.surface: A creature, dreadfully thin, eventually perished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns LEAN into ELAN; 'finally' takes D from 'died'.
explanation.definitionFit: This large African antelope is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Imparter of knowledge, in-class worker

parts.note: in class, as a sportsman on good form, is in form
the worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A teacher who is also a hard-working member of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imparter of knowledge' suggests a teacher, but it is someone who passes information, often to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gives information, especially to the authorities, imparts knowledge to them.

clue.text: Potential source of energy, and other things, in plentiful supply

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for and other things inside the word for a plentiful supply

parts.note: a well is a plentiful source or supply, as of knowledge
etc, short for et cetera, means and other things

explanation.surface: An energy source and assorted other things, all in abundant supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potential' hints at electrical potential rather than mere possibility: the answer is a battery cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery cell with liquid electrolyte stores electrical potential, so it is a possible energy source.

clue.text: Turn out always on time

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A command to show up regularly and punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: To evert is to turn something inside out, so it is a technical synonym of turn out.

clue.text: Old British retainer keeping close eye on things on things

parts.note: a retainer is a household servant of long standing

explanation.surface: An old British manservant who keeps a careful watch on the household.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'on things' at the end appears to be a printing duplication; the clue reads correctly with one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being watchful, noticing everything around you, is what keeping a close eye on things means.

clue.text: What's provided in late afternoon?

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words late afternoon

explanation.surface: A question about what gets served as the day winds down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the meal and the three letters also sit across 'late afternoon'.
explanation.definitionFit: The light meal served around four o'clock is the British afternoon refreshment.

clue.text: Type article alongside photo

parts.note: pic is short for picture or photo
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A printer setting an article next to a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Pica is a size of printing type, twelve points, so it is a kind of type.

clue.text: Twenty-four hours of pop?

parts.note: a day belonging to pop, where pop is dad rather than music or fizzy drink

explanation.surface: A day-long stretch of pop music on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' suggests pop music, but it means dad.
explanation.definitionFit: This annual June celebration honours fathers, so it is a whole day devoted to dad.

clue.text: Type of petrol put in van available for hire

parts.note: to put someone in the van, at the front, is to have them lead
a taxi showing its light is free, available for hire

explanation.surface: Fuel poured into a rental van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' looks like a vehicle but is the vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Unleaded petrol, made without added lead, is the type described.

clue.text: Change of direction almost crucial for would-be EC member

indicators.note: almost cuts the closing letter from the word for a change of direction

parts.note: a turn is a change of direction
key means crucial or vital

explanation.surface: A political U-turn that is vital for a country hoping to join Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops N from TURN. The EC was the European Community, which this country long hoped to join.
explanation.definitionFit: This country applied to join the European Community and remained a long-standing candidate.

clue.text: Anticipating having to swallow yellow cough medicine?

indicators.note: having to swallow means one word takes in another

parts.note: expectant means anticipating or waiting hopefully
or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: Someone expecting to have to take a sickly yellow cough syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: The heraldic term for gold supplies the yellow; the question mark flags that the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine that helps bring up phlegm is a kind of cough remedy, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Accept less damaged glasses

indicators.note: damaged signals that the letters of accept less are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Settling for broken spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the ten letters of ACCEPT LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the frames with lenses worn to correct eyesight, another word for glasses.

clue.text: Criminal investigators arresting working class groups

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so one word holds the others inside it

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, treated here as investigators
on means working or functioning, as a machine is on
a sort is a class or kind

explanation.surface: Detectives detaining a band of manual workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The US intelligence agency stands in loosely for criminal investigators; 'working class' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: These are associations of companies combined for a venture, so groups or syndicates.

clue.text: One creature after another steps on sailing vessel

parts.note: a seal is a sea creature
another creature: the adder, a snake

explanation.surface: Animals filing on board a ship one after the other, like Noah's ark.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAL comes first, then 'another' creature, ADDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or rigid ladder hung from a ship's side gives steps for climbing aboard.

clue.text: A politician's current measures

parts.note: MP's, belonging to a Member of Parliament, a politician

explanation.surface: A politician's up-to-date policies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like present-day but is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of electric current are measured in these, short for amperes.

clue.text: Slight reduction in financial aid is relative

indicators.note: a slight reduction means losing just one letter from the end

parts.note: a grant is financial aid

explanation.surface: A small cut in funding is related to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight reduction in' drops the last letter, T, from GRANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandmother, shortened, is a family member, hence a relative.

clue.text: See bad artist etch four lines

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of artist etch are put in a poor, scrambled order

explanation.surface: Watching an incompetent artist make an etching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges the ten letters of ARTIST ETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: This poetic term names a stanza or poem made of four lines, a quatrain.

clue.text: Paint from Ulster?

parts.note: an ulster is a heavy overcoat, so the paint layer sits on top like an outer coat

explanation.surface: Asking about paint made in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulster' looks like the province, but an ulster is a long overcoat, a coat worn on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The final layer of paint applied over the undercoat is known by this name.

clue.text: Repulsed, displays temper tantrums

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the word for displays is read backwards

parts.note: to sport something is to display or wear it proudly

explanation.surface: Disgusted, a person shows fits of rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repulsed' reverses SPORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A strop is a fit of sulking bad temper, a tantrum in British slang.

clue.text: Breezes getting up about end of day in the country

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another
getting up in a down clue means the word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: airs are light breezes

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the word day

explanation.surface: Winds rising at dusk across the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns AIRS to SRIA; 'about' puts it round Y from 'end of day'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Middle Eastern nation, so it is a country.

clue.text: Secretly place drug in Daphne's first home?

parts.note: to plant is to place something secretly, as evidence
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A tale of someone hiding drugs in Daphne's house.
explanation.walkthrough: Daphne is a shrub, so its first home might be a pot before planting out.
explanation.definitionFit: A daphne is a garden plant, and its earliest home is a container for growing plants.

clue.text: Secret society linked to a group of islands

parts.note: a tong is a Chinese secret society

explanation.surface: A secret society connected to an archipelago.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific kingdom is an archipelago, a group of islands in Polynesia.

clue.text: Control young outlaw

parts.note: master is the old title for a young boy
Robin Hood is the famous outlaw

explanation.surface: A command to restrain a teenage criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young outlaw' looks like one idea, a juvenile delinquent, but splits into a boy's title and Robin's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being master, having command, is control or mastery.

clue.text: Bend regularly eliminating characters in car race

indicators.note: regularly eliminating means every other letter of car race is dropped, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: A racing driver taking a curve.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop C, R, A, E from 'car race' to leave A, R, C.
explanation.definitionFit: A curve or bow in a line is a bend.

clue.text: Husband leaves Welsh place in good order

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so one letter is taken out

parts.note: Neath is a town in South Wales

explanation.surface: A man walking out of his home in Wales, tidily.
explanation.walkthrough: NEATH is a town in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy and orderly is the meaning of this adjective.

clue.text: With daily performance at rep, developed skill in role

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning lady, also called a char
an act is a performance

indicators.note: developed signals that the letters of rep are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: An actor in repertory theatre honing their craft through daily shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges REP to ERP. A daily is British for a cleaner, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a theatrical role portraying an eccentric or distinctive person.
